title: What are the other angles of symmetry of a square?
description: A square lands on itself after a ninety degree turn. A half turn, a three quarter turn and a full turn also make it overlap itself. Keeko's doubt is that only the quarter turn works, because a half turn turns the square upside down.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square overlaps itself after every multiple of a quarter turn, which gives one hundred and eighty, two hundred and seventy and three hundred and sixty degrees besides ninety. Watch for students who think an upside down square is a different picture.

source: What are the other angles of symmetry of a square (besides 9
video_script.why: The child turns the square by a half turn, a three quarter turn and a full turn, and sees that it overlaps itself each time.
video_script.substitution: Turn the square by two, three and four quarter turns and check that it overlaps itself each time.
video_script.anchor: a square with a red dot at its centre and a small dot at each corner
video_script.wrong_answer: only the quarter turn works, because a half turn turns the square upside down
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says only the quarter turn works, because a half turn turns the square upside down. A square looks the same upside down, because its four sides are equal and the top side fits where the bottom side was.
video_script.payoff_line: The other angles of symmetry are the half turn, the three quarter turn and the full turn

final_answer.spoken: the other angles of symmetry are the half turn, the three quarter turn and the full turn

maths_rules: A turn about the centre after which a shape looks exactly the same is called an angle of symmetry
Two quarter turns make a half turn: 2 x 90 = 180 degrees
Three quarter turns make a three quarter turn: 3 x 90 = 270 degrees
Four quarter turns make the full turn: 4 x 90 = 360 degrees
A square overlaps itself after each of these turns, because its four sides and four corners are equal
video_script.design: One idea: a square overlaps itself after two, three and four quarter turns. The square stays on the board all video. Wrong idea: only the quarter turn works, because the half turn makes the square upside down.
